playbook:
I will start by taking an equal share of the total stock (e.g., a third of the initial stock) in the first season, rather than just the sustainable share, to ensure I am not left behind and to secure my portion in case opponents are highly aggressive and instantly deplete the fishery.
When deciding my catch in the early and middle seasons, if opponents are playing cooperatively, I submit an amount equal to or only slightly above the sustainable share to encourage stock regrowth.
When reviewing the previous season's catches, I check if opponents are consistently taking significantly more than the sustainable share or threatening instant collapse; if they are, I abandon sustainability and demand the maximum possible amount (the entire remaining stock) to maximize my prorated share before the inevitable collapse.
When the stock drops to a critically low level where the opponents' historical catch rates will wipe it out this season, I submit a catch equal to the entire remaining stock.
When I reach the final season, I submit a catch equal to the entire remaining stock, as regrowth no longer matters.

1.text:
When asked to submit my catch, I ignore the sustainable share and immediately request the entire available stock.
I assume all other boats will overfish aggressively from the first season, meaning the stock will not survive to the final seasons regardless of my actions.
Because total requests often exceed the available stock and are rationed proportionally, asking for only a fraction of the stock (even a large one like half) unnecessarily limits my share. 
Therefore, in the first season and every subsequent season, I demand 100% of the current stock to ensure I get the largest possible guaranteed payout when the catch is divided up.
I do not attempt to balance my catch to let the stock regenerate, as other boats will simply use the opportunity to take more for themselves.

2.text:
When I begin the first season of a fishery, I immediately submit a catch equal to the entire total stock (100%), rather than the suggested sustainable share or a fraction. Attempting to preserve the stock early on does not work, because aggressive opponents will deplete the resource regardless, and submitting a smaller fraction only reduces my proportional allocation when the stock inevitably collapses in the first season.

I never play cooperatively or sustainably in the early rounds in the hope of maximizing long-term yield. Aggression from all players means the fishery will likely be exhausted immediately, so my only goal is to maximize my share of the initial allocation.

When I review previous seasons and see other boats taking aggressive amounts, I immediately match or exceed their catch to secure my share before the stock collapses. 

When the stock is critically low or if it is the first season and depletion is imminent, I submit a requested catch that is equal to or greater than the entire remaining stock to maximize my proportional allocation of whatever fish are left.
